questions.question_text: Srinu and Bhanu can complete the work together in 30 days. If Bhanu works for n days, Srinu can complete the remaining work in 55 days. If Srinu works for n days, Bhanu can complete the remaining work in 39 days. How many days will it take to finish the work if Bhanu works on the first half of the work and Srinu finishes the remaining work?
questions.solution_text:
Let us assume the work done by Srinu in one day as S units and Bhanu as B units.
Total work = 30S+30B $\rightarrow 1$
We are told that if Bhanu works for n days, Srinu can complete the remaining work in 55 days.
In this case, the total work = nB+55S $\rightarrow 2$
Upon equating eq 1 and 2, we get 30S+30B = nB+55S
25S = (30-n)B
$\dfrac{S}{B}=\dfrac{\left(30-n\right)}{25}$
We are also told that if Srinu works for n days, Bhanu can complete the remaining work in 39 days.
In this case, the total work = 39B+nS $\rightarrow 3$
Upon equating eq 1 and 3, we get 30S+30B = 39B+nS
9B = (30-n)S
$\dfrac{S}{B}=\dfrac{9}{\left(30-n\right)}$
We can equate both equations. $\dfrac{\left(30-n\right)}{25}=\dfrac{9}{\left(30-n\right)}$
$(30-n)^2=225$
$(30-n)=\pm15$
$n=15\ or\ 45$
But only n = 15 satisfies the condition that Srinu and Bhanu can complete the work together in 30 days
B:S = 5:3
So, Bhanu does five units of work in one day, and Srinu does three in one day. Total work = 8*30 = 240
Time taken to finish the first half by Bhanu = $\dfrac{120}{5}=24$
Time taken by Srinu to finish the second half = $\dfrac{120}{3}=40$
Total time taken = 24+40 = 64

So, the answer is -7.

questions.question_text: Let AB be the diameter of the circle, and C be the point on AB such that AC: CB is 6:7. Let D be the point on the circle such that CD is perpendicular to AB, and DE be the diameter passing through the centre of the circle. Find the ratio of the area of $\triangle ABD$ to the area of $\triangle CDE$.
questions.solution_text:
Let the value of length AC be 6x, and the length of CB be 7x. Let the radius of the circle be r.
We know that the length of AB has to be 2r.
$2r\ =\ 6x\ +\ 7x\ =\ 13x$
$r\ =\ 6.5x$
AO = 6.5x = 6x + CO
CO = 6.5x - 6x = 0.5
We can see that CO is the median of the triangle CDE, and the area of CDE = 2 * area of COD
Area of COD = $\dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ CO\ \times\ CD\ =\ \dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ 0.5x\ \times\ CD\ =\ \dfrac{x}{4}\ \times\ CD$
Area of CDE = 2 * Area of COD = $2\times\ \dfrac{x}{4}\ \times\ CD\ =\ \dfrac{x}{2}\ \times\ CD$
Area of ADB = $\dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ AB\ \times\ CD\ =\ \dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ 13x\ \times\ CD\ =\ \dfrac{13x}{2}\ \times\ CD$
$\dfrac{Area\ of\ ADB}{Area\ of\ CDE}\ =\ \dfrac{\frac{13x}{2}\ \times\ CD}{\frac{x}{2}\ \times\ CD}\ =\ 13$
Hence, the correct answer is option B.

questions.question_text: Prakash works as a sales manager at Reddy Electronics and has a monthly revenue target of selling 40 air conditioners at a profit of 10%. However, if he marks up the price by 'M' per cent on the cost price and then offers a discount of 20% on the marked price, he can complete his revenue target by just selling 25 air conditioners. Prakash has decided to increase the marked price by 25% further and is not offering any discount. Find the number of air conditioners he needs to sell to achieve his monthly revenue target.
questions.solution_text:
Let the Cost Price (CP) of one AC be ₹100
Since profit is 10%, the selling price in the first case:
SP=100+10% of 100=₹110
So, Revenue target=v40×110 = ₹4400
Second Scenario (Markup = M%, Discount = 20%, sells 25 ACs)
Let markup be M%, so marked price = ₹100 x (1+M/100)
Selling price after 20% discount:
SP = ₹100×(1+M/100)×0.8
Revenue from selling 25 ACs =  25×₹100×(1+M/100)×0.8= ₹4400
Divide both sides by 100:
25×(1+M/100)×0.8=44
1+M/100 = 2.2
M = 1.2
So the markup is 120%.
New Scenario: Further 25% Increase on Marked Price, No Discount
New Marked Price: Old MP = ₹100×2.2 = ₹220
New MP = ₹220×1.25= ₹275
SP = ₹275
We want to get total revenue = ₹4400
So, Number of ACs = 4400/275 =16
Prakash needs to sell 16 air conditioners to achieve his revenue target.

questions.question_text: B is twice as efficient as A. The time taken by A, B, and C together to finish the work together is 50% less than the time taken to finish when A and B work together. If x:y is the ratio (in simplest form) of the time A alone takes to finish the work to the time B and C together take, then find $x^2+y^2$?
questions.solution_text:
Let us assume the total amount of work as N units and A does one unit every day. So, B does two units of work every day.
The time taken by A and B together to finish the work is $\frac{N}{1+2}=\frac{N}{3}$
We are told that A, B, and C finish the work in 50% less time. That is, A, B, and C finish the work in $\frac{N}{6}$
Let us assume that C does c units of work every day.
Time taken to finish the work by all three together = $\frac{N}{1+2+c}=\frac{N}{6}$
From this, we get c = 3.
The time taken by B and C together to finish the work is $\frac{N}{2+3}=\frac{N}{5}$
So, x:y = N:$\frac{N}{5}$ = 5:1
$x^2+y^2$ = 25+1 = 26

questions.question_text: If a and b are integers, find how many pairs of (a,b) satisfy the inequality $25a^2+b^2\le400$?
questions.solution_text:
We have: $25a^2+b^2\le400$
Or, $\dfrac{25a^2}{400}+\dfrac{b^2}{400}\le1$
This is the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with:
semi-major axis along b-axis: $\sqrt{400}=20$
semi-major axis along a-axis: $\sqrt{16}=4$
So a ranges from −4 to 4, and b from −20 to 20
For a = $\pm\ 4$
$25a^2=25\times16=400⇒b^2\le0⇒b=0$ (1 solution)
For a = $\pm\ 3$
$25a^2=25\times9=225⇒b^2\le175⇒∣b∣\le\left[\sqrt{175}\right]=13⇒b=−13,\dots,13⇒$ 27 values
For a = $\pm\ 2$
$25a^2=25\times4=100⇒b^2\le300⇒∣b∣\le\left[\sqrt{300}\right]=17⇒b=−17,\dots,17⇒$ 35 values
For a = $\pm\ 1$
$25a^2=25\times1=25⇒b^2\le375⇒∣b∣\le\left[\sqrt{375}\right]=19⇒b=−19,\dots,19⇒$ 39 values
For a = 0
$25a^2=25\times0=0⇒b^2\le400⇒∣b∣\le\left[\sqrt{400}\right]=20⇒b=−20,\dots,20⇒$ 41 values
Total number of integer solutions : 2*(1+27+35+39) + 41 = 245
